chunks: What Sahl ibn Ziyād narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Rayyān, who said:

I wrote to him, peace be upon him: A man may be inside a house whose walls prevent him from seeing the redness of the west, from knowing the disappearance of the twilight, and from knowing the time of the later ʿishāʾ prayer. When should he perform it, and what should he do?

So he, peace be upon him, wrote: He should perform it, when he is in this condition, at the time when the stars become few to see; and he should perform maghrib at the time of their intermingling and the whiteness of the sun’s setting.

And we have already stated that the end of the time of maghrib is the disappearance of the twilight, which is the redness from the direction of the west. And what some reports contain, that it extends to a quarter of the night, is to be understood as applying to those with excuses; and we have cited the reports concerning that, and this further clarifies it.

key_terms.أَصْحَابِ الْأَعْذَارِ: those who have valid excuses affecting the normal ruling
key_terms.اشْتِبَاكِهَا: the intermingling or dense appearance of the stars as an indicator
key_terms.حُمْرَةِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the redness in the western horizon used to identify prayer time
key_terms.قَصْرِ النُّجُومِ: the reduction or faintness of visible stars as a timing sign
key_terms.مَغِيبِ الشَّفَقِ: the disappearance of twilight marking the end of maghrib time

ai.seo_question: How should maghrib and ʿishāʾ prayer times be determined if the horizon cannot be seen?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling for determining the times of maghrib and ʿishāʾ when a person cannot directly observe the western horizon because of surrounding walls. It gives practical indicators based on the stars and twilight, and clarifies that the normal end of maghrib is the disappearance of the western redness, while reports extending it further apply to those with valid excuses.
